I will keep doing what has worked for me, but I will stay a little tighter with inputs because I am 67 now, my family labor is only 2 people, and I have to manage 33 mu in a way that is steady and not too risky. Since my land already follows a wheat-maize system and I have well irrigation, I will keep most of the land in wheat followed by summer maize, because that is the safest way for me to get grain from the same fields in a normal year. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because I still grow it and I know how to manage it, but I will not expand it because cotton takes more picking and more field watching. I will use better seed where it helps me most, especially for maize and wheat, because I want stable emergence and yield. I will fertilize wheat and maize more heavily than cotton, irrigate wheat the most because it responds well to water here, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage so the work is easier for me and my household. I will spray only as much as I think is necessary to protect the crop, because too much costs money and too little risks yield. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield, but to get a dependable harvest from each mu with work I can actually finish.
